concepts.name: Background and Causes of Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
key_dimensions: Unjustified 22% revenue hike by Bombay Presidency despite poor agrarian conditions
Post-WWI economic distress, falling cotton prices, and drought conditions in Surat district
Earlier aborted 1922 Bardoli Satyagraha and its connection to the 1928 movement
Role of Maxwell-Broomfield Committee report and its findings on revenue revision

concepts.name: Vallabhbhai Patel's Leadership and Organizational Role
key_dimensions: Patel's selection as leader over other Congress figures and his administrative acumen
Formation of village-level volunteer corps and communication networks
Patel's strategy of non-violent non-cooperation including tax refusal
How Bardoli earned Patel the title 'Sardar' — who conferred it and under what circumstances

concepts.name: Title 'Sardar' — Origin and Significance
key_dimensions: Conferred by women of Bardoli (not Gandhi, a common UPSC trap) upon Vallabhbhai Patel
Political symbolism of the title in the context of peasant leadership
Distinction between popular titles conferred during movements vs. official honors
Comparison with Gandhi's 'Mahatma' title — both conferred by people, not institutions

concepts.name: Gandhian Methods and Non-Violence in Bardoli
key_dimensions: Application of Satyagraha principles: non-payment of revenue, social boycott of informers
Bardoli as a 'laboratory' for testing Gandhian mass mobilization techniques
Distinction between Bardoli's peaceful conduct vs. other contemporary agrarian movements involving violence
Gandhi's role as moral overseer vs. Patel's role as operational commander

concepts.name: Role of Women in Bardoli Satyagraha
key_dimensions: Active participation of women in picketing, marches, and moral pressure campaigns
Women's role in conferring the title 'Sardar' on Patel — political agency of women
Comparison with women's participation in Civil Disobedience Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement
Bardoli as an early precedent for mainstreaming women in Gandhian mass movements

concepts.name: Government Response: Repression and Confiscation
key_dimensions: Attachment and auction of lands and cattle of defaulting peasants
Social solidarity tactics used by peasants to nullify auction sales
Role of neighboring district peasants and traders in refusing to buy confiscated property
Bombay government's miscalculation of the movement's resilience

concepts.name: Settlement and Outcome: The Bombay Government's Capitulation
key_dimensions: Terms of the settlement: revenue enhancement withdrawn and confiscated lands restored
Role of Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry commission in validating peasants' demands
Significance of government restoring lands — a rare concession in colonial agrarian history
Distinction: revenue was not permanently abolished but the specific unjust hike was reversed

concepts.name: Bardoli Satyagraha vs. Other Contemporary Peasant Movements
key_dimensions: Comparison with Kheda Satyagraha (1918) — both led by Gandhi/Patel, both over revenue, different outcomes
Contrast with Moplah Rebellion (1921) — violence vs. non-violence in agrarian grievances
Contrast with Tebhaga and Telangana movements — class ideology vs. Gandhian nationalism
Bardoli's unique feature: purely non-violent peasant movement with a successful outcome

concepts.name: Bardoli Satyagraha and the Indian National Congress
key_dimensions: Congress's cautious endorsement vs. direct leadership — distinction between party support and party-led movement
How Bardoli's success influenced Congress's strategy ahead of Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)
Bardoli as a rehearsal for mass civil disobedience at the national level
Gandhi's statement declaring Bardoli 'the first decisive battle for India's independence'

concepts.name: Kheda Satyagraha (1918) vs. Bardoli Satyagraha (1928): Comparative Analysis
key_dimensions: Both involved revenue disputes in Gujarat; Kheda led by Gandhi, Bardoli led by Patel
Kheda outcome was ambiguous (partial relief); Bardoli had a clear peasant victory
Different levels of peasant organization and Congress machinery in 1918 vs. 1928
UPSC trap: confusing the two Gujarat satyagrahas in terms of leader, year, and outcome

concepts.name: Geographical and Socioeconomic Context of Bardoli Taluka
key_dimensions: Location in Surat district of Bombay Presidency — not a standalone district
Predominantly Koli and Kunbi peasant communities alongside tribal populations
Economic dependence on cotton cultivation and vulnerability to market fluctuations
Bardoli's prior association with 1922 proposed satyagraha that was called off by Gandhi post-Chauri Chaura

concepts.name: Revenue Settlement System and Colonial Agrarian Policy
key_dimensions: Ryotwari system operative in Bombay Presidency — direct peasant-state relationship without zamindars
How periodic revenue settlements created vulnerability to arbitrary enhancements
The 22% hike as violation of settlement norms and its administrative illegitimacy
Comparison with Permanent Settlement areas — why Bardoli-type movements were specific to ryotwari zones

concepts.name: Role of Media and Propaganda in Bardoli
key_dimensions: K.M. Munshi and other Congress publicists highlighting the movement in national press
Gandhi's newspaper 'Young India' as a platform for building national sympathy
Information blackout attempts by colonial government vs. Congress's counter-narrative
Bardoli as an early example of media-managed nationalist agitation

concepts.name: Participation of Non-Peasant Groups: Merchants, Lawyers, and Tribals
key_dimensions: Local merchants refusing to buy attached property — economic solidarity as a weapon
Lawyers boycotting colonial courts in sympathy — broader civil society participation
Tribal communities (Dublas, Halpatis) participation alongside landowning peasants
Cross-class unity as a distinguishing feature of Bardoli vs. purely class-based movements

concepts.name: Bardoli Satyagraha as a Model for Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)
key_dimensions: Organizational templates from Bardoli (village units, volunteer corps) replicated nationally in 1930
Patel's administrative lessons from Bardoli applied during Salt March preparations
Gandhi's deliberate study of Bardoli's success before launching nationwide disobedience
UPSC angle: Bardoli as a 'bridge' movement between Non-Cooperation (1920-22) and Civil Disobedience (1930)

concepts.name: Ideological Underpinnings: Class Struggle vs. Nationalist Framing
key_dimensions: Gandhi's insistence on framing Bardoli as nationalist duty, not class war against landlords
Absence of socialist/Marxist ideology distinguishing Bardoli from Tebhaga or Telangana
How the nationalist framing helped gain broader middle-class support but limited radical agrarian reform
Left critique of Bardoli: addressing tax grievances without challenging land ownership structures

concepts.name: Legacy and Long-term Impact of Bardoli Satyagraha
key_dimensions: Establishment of Patel as a national leader and future Congress strongman
Demonstration that non-violent mass movements could extract concrete economic concessions from colonial state
Influence on agrarian policy debates in the late colonial period and post-independence land reform discourse
Bardoli's symbolic status in Gujarat's political identity and its invocation in contemporary politics

concepts.name: Bardoli Satyagraha and Gandhi-Patel Relationship
key_dimensions: Division of roles: Gandhi as ideological guide, Patel as field commander
Gandhi's trust in Patel demonstrated by choosing him over senior Congress leaders
How Bardoli shaped the Gandhi-Patel dynamic that lasted through the independence movement
Contrast with Gandhi-Nehru relationship — Patel's pragmatism vs. Nehru's idealism, both evident from Bardoli

concepts.name: Aborted 1922 Bardoli Satyagraha: Context and Significance
key_dimensions: Gandhi had selected Bardoli for first mass civil disobedience before Chauri Chaura (February 1922)
Withdrawal after Chauri Chaura violence — Bardoli thus linked to Non-Cooperation Movement's suspension
How the 1922 aborted plan created organizational groundwork exploited successfully in 1928
UPSC trap: confusing 1922 planned (but cancelled) Bardoli satyagraha with 1928 actual movement

concepts.name: Social Boycott as a Weapon in Bardoli: Methods and Effectiveness
key_dimensions: Boycott of informers, government servants, and auction participants by village communities
Use of social ostracism (not violence) to enforce solidarity — distinctly Gandhian mechanism
Effectiveness of social boycott in rural context vs. its limitations in urban industrial disputes
Ethical debates within the movement about coercive aspects of social boycott vs. voluntary non-cooperation
